title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the Lemma of the previous page (ms. p. 455). Setting: M is an Azumaya algebra of rank 4 over a base S, and G = M^× is the associated form of GL(2). PG is its projective group and SG its determinant-1 subgroup. σ is a section of G. A_σ is the scheme of y in SG with Tr(yσ) = Tr σ. The lemma states that the following are equivalent: (a) A_σ is stable under y ↦ εy for ε in μ_2; (b) Tr σ = 0; (c) a normal form σ = (0 −1; −ν 0), equivalently w = 1 in the earlier parametrization of ρ, σ. It also asserts these imply (d) σ² is a scalar, i.e. the image σ̃ in PG is an involution.

The page finishes b) ⇔ d) using Hamilton–Cayley, σ² − (Tr σ)σ + det σ·1 = 0.
- If Tr σ = 0, then σ² = −det σ·1, a scalar.
- Conversely, if σ² is scalar, then (Tr σ)σ = σ² + det σ·1 is scalar. When σ is not scalar in any fibre, 1 and σ span a locally free rank-2 direct summand of M. So the coefficient Tr σ must vanish.

This is the standard fact that a non-scalar element of PGL2 has order 2 iff its lifts have trace 0. It is the 'order 2' half of normalizing the images of the generators ρ (order 3) and σ (order 2) of PSL2(Z) = Z/3 * Z/2 inside a form of PGL2.

Under these conditions Grothendieck then defines (8): G*_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G × G × E' × E', the scheme of solutions (α, β, μ, ε) of the 'loop equation' (2). In (2) a sign ε appears because a lift of the involution σ̃ to G is only defined up to μ_2. He also defines (9): G̃*_{ρ,σ} ⊂ PG × PG × E', the solutions (α, β, μ) of the projective equation (1). Projection onto the last factor gives (10): ε : G*_{ρ,σ} → μ_2.

The next page shows how the construction continues:
- ε factors through the projective version.
- The 'honest' solution scheme G_{ρ,σ} is ε⁻¹(1).
- Via (α, β) ↦ (ξ = αρ(α)⁻¹, η = εβσ(β)⁻¹), the solution schemes fibre over X_{ρ,σ} × μ_2.

Purpose: in 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets', Grothendieck studies the solution schemes of the loop (Teichmüller/GT-type) equations with values in (forms of) GL2/PGL2. He handles the μ_2 sign ambiguity coming from the order-2 generator.
errors: First line as written, 'Tr σ = 0 ⇒ σ = det σ·1', is a slip. Hamilton–Cayley gives σ² = −det σ·1 (a scalar), not σ itself scalar.
'(Tr σ)σ = σ² − det σ·1' has a sign error. From σ² − (Tr σ)σ + det σ = 0 one gets (Tr σ)σ = σ² + det σ·1. This is harmless for the argument.

The converse needs σ to be non-scalar in every fibre so that 1 and σ are fibrewise independent. Grothendieck flags this himself in the parenthesis ('si σ n'est un scalaire en aucune fibre'), so it is a stated hypothesis, not a gap.

ideas.what: For a non-scalar 2x2 matrix (section of an Azumaya algebra of rank 4), σ² is scalar iff Tr σ = 0, via Cayley–Hamilton; i.e. the involutions of PGL2 are the images of the trace-zero elements.
ideas.modern_name: Cayley–Hamilton characterization of involutions in PGL2 / forms of PGL2

ideas.what: Introducing a μ_2-valued sign ε in the loop equation to account for lifting an order-2 element of PG to G, giving the solution scheme G* with ε: G* → μ_2, honest solutions = ε⁻¹(1), and a factorization through the projective solution scheme.
ideas.modern_name: lifting obstruction / μ_2-twist in a central extension GL2 → PGL2 for representations of PSL2(Z)-type relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard central-extension bookkeeping; specific setting unpublished

ideas.what: Studying solution schemes of the 'loop equation' (Teichmüller-tower / GT-type relations attached to the generators ρ, σ of PSL2(Z)) with values in forms of GL2 over a general base
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT group: Drinfeld 1990 and Ihara; Grothendieck's program in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the Teichmüller tower; this GL2-valued variant appears only in the Longue Marche-related manuscripts as far as known

missed.claim: Part of an unpublished, systematic study of solution schemes of the loop equation with values in forms of GL2 (Azumaya algebras) over arbitrary bases, including the μ_2-sign refinement. The present page itself only contains routine lemmas and definitions.
missed.quote: le schéma des solutions en (α,β,μ,ε) de l'équation (2) ... fournit un morphisme G*_{ρ,σ} --ε--> μ_2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: GL2-valued solutions of GT/loop equations connect to monodromy representations of the projective line minus three points and to GT actions. The scheme-theoretic treatment of these solution spaces may be little explored in print; the page alone is too routine to establish novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is an elementary Cayley–Hamilton argument plus definitions of solution schemes with a μ_2 sign. It is interesting only as context for Grothendieck's unpublished GL2-valued study of the loop equation.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the manuscript indeed reads 'σ = detσ.1' (an author's slip for σ² = −det σ·1); the transcription is faithful to the image.
Line 3: the manuscript writes '(Trσ)σ = σ² − detσ.1'; faithful, but mathematically it should be '+'.
The illegible parenthesis likely reads '(si σ n'est en aucune fibre un scalaire)'.
Crossed-out line before (8): 'soit alors que le schéma G_{ρ,σ} des (α,β,μ,ε) satisfaisant' is struck through.
Line after (8): plausibly 'qui est aussi l'image inverse dans G×G×E'×E' du schéma G̃*_{ρ,σ}'.
'projection sur le [deuxième] facteur E'' — 'deuxième' is struck; the target factor is the last E' (the ε coordinate).
